entities.summary: The St. Nicholas Church is the main church of the Kotka Orthodox Church in Kotka, Finland, surrounded by the Isopuisto park The church was built between 1799 and 1801 according to the drawings of architect Jakov Perrin. The church dates back to the time of the active years of the sea fortress of Ruotsinsalmi, when the Russians built the Ruotsinsalmi–Kyminlinna double fortress in the Kymi parish and a fortress town was created on Kotkansaari. The church is the oldest building in present-day Kotka, and it is a notable representative of neoclassicism in Finland. Saint Nicholas Church in Kotka is a church building in Europe, established in 1799. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Established in 1799, Saint Nicholas Church in Kotka played a significant role in the development of Finnish architecture during the neoclassical period. Its construction coincided with the creation of the Ruotsinsalmi–Kyminlinna double fortress, reflecting the strategic importance of the region.
